basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Qui Jectan genuit Helmodad, et Saleph, et Asarmoth, Jare et Adura et Uzal Decha, et Ebal,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Qui Jectan genuit Helmodad, et Saleph, et Asarmoth, Jare et Adura et Uzal Decha, et Ebal, et Abimael, Saba et Ophir, et Evila, et Jobab. Omnes isti filii Jectan. Harum gentium posteriora nomina Hieronymus se invenire non potuisse testatur. « Sed usque in praesens, inquit, quia procul a nobis sunt, vel ita vocantur ut primum, vel quae immutata sunt ignorantur. » Legimus autem supra quia Phison unus de quatuor paradisi fluminibus, quem nostri Gangen vocant, et esse in India non dubitatur, circumeat omnem terram Evilath; quae videlicet terra ab hoc Evila nomen accepisse videtur. Narrat enim eum Josephus cum fratribus suis a fluvio Coephere omnem Indiae regionem quae vocatur Hieira possedisse, sed et Verba dierum narrant quia servi Salomonis per mare Rubrum abierunt in Ophir, et attulerunt inde aurum, et ligna thina, et gemmas pretiosissimas, quae esse Indiae regio, et ab Ophir filio Jectan vocabulum traxisse, credibile est.
